grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: ひろいです。ひろいへやです。しずかです。しずかなへやです。

tables.caption: The i-adjective keeps い in both positions
The na-adjective uses な immediately before a noun
Doing something to a door and the door’s result

grammar.note_en:
An adjective describes a noun. In a predicate it tells us something about the topic: ここはひろいです means “It is spacious here.” Before a noun, it identifies which kind of thing we mean: ひろいへや means “a spacious room.” These are polite nonpast descriptions. This chapter teaches the demonstrated present descriptions and noun modifiers, not adjective past or adjective negative paradigms. Known verb past remains available when Ren recalls borrowing the chair.

The first group is called i-adjectives. Their final い remains in both positions: ひろいです / ひろいへや, “It is spacious / a spacious room”; くらいです / くらいへや, “It is dark / a dark room”; あかるいです / あかるいへや, “It is bright / a bright room.” Do not put な between one of these adjectives and its noun. The already familiar おおきい and ちいさい spellings in the story have the same adjective behaviour; practice keeps their kana spelling. Other new i-adjectives here are せまい “cramped,” ふるい “old” and あたらしい “new.”

The second group is called na-adjectives because な links them directly to a following noun. Compare しずかです / しずかなへや, “It is quiet / a quiet room”; きれいです / きれいなつくえ, “It is clean / a clean table”; べんりです / べんりなつくえ, “It is convenient / a convenient table”; にぎやかです / にぎやかなあつまり, “It is lively / a lively gathering.” Use な before the noun, not before です. Although きれい ends in the kana い, it belongs to this second group: its demonstrated noun form is きれいな, not a rule inferred from spelling alone. Here きれい means clean, the sense used for the room, table and chairs.

The story evaluates two different needs without teaching a comparative construction. The small room is bright and clean, but the chairs block its entrance when the volunteers try to seat everyone. The other room has floor space for the gathering but little window light. Switching on its electric light makes the table usable for reading. The actual arrangement uses the spacious room for books and the small bright room for tea. Adjacent descriptions and practical actions establish the contrast; there is no new “more than” or “most” form to memorise.

たくさんのひと means “many people.” たりません means “there are not enough”: いすがたりません is “There are not enough chairs.” It is the whole taught polite form, not a new general numeral or counter series. すわります uses に for the seat: いすにすわります means “sit in a chair.” つかいます takes を for the thing used: ひろいへやをつかいます means “We use the spacious room.” でんきをつけます means “switch on the electric light.” The reading scene demonstrates the light’s practical consequence.

Opening has two different verb patterns. とびらをあけます means “open the door”: a person acts on the door, marked by を. とびらはあきます means “the door opens”: the door itself is the topic. とだなのとびらはあきません means “the cupboard door does not open.” It reports a failed result after the characters pull the doors, not a newly taught potential verb meaning “cannot open.” とびらをひきます means “pull the door” in these actions. The working room entrance and the cupboard are separate; possession of the room key does not establish a cupboard key or reveal its contents.

The kanji stage writes the already known whole hour さんじ with authored readings, followed by the taught half-hour element はん. The chapter does not derive an unrestricted cardinal series or other hour readings. The new go/come spellings are spellings of the known whole polite words いきます and きます. Every story kanji retains authored readings. The two previously taught date expressions remain entirely in kana: their conventional whole kanji forms need more characters than this five-character stage introduces. Practice, vocabulary citations and card fronts stay in kana.

obrazec.rule: Worked model: the agreed time in this chapter’s opening. Then retrieve these stages: 1 first chair trial in the small room; 2 reading after the light is on; 3 room-use plan for tea; 4 chair borrowing; 5 both cupboard-door attempts; 6 final room arrangement. items.rubric: Section 1 first chair trial: Ren remains at the doorway while the others sit and a chair occupies that entrance. He enters after the blocking chair is moved. Describe the first trial, not the cleared doorway at its end.

model_answers: れんは、みせでいすをかります。
items.rubric: Section 3: Ren borrows a new chair at the shop, then returns with it. Accept an equivalent complete sentence with the narrative nonpast or correctly recalled past for that completed borrowing.

items.rubric: Section4: both people pull the cupboard doors, not the working room entrance. Give a complete sentence identifying the cupboard doors; an additional sentence may say they do not open. Do not invent the contents.

model_answers: ほんは、ひろいへやでよみます。おちゃは、ちいさいへやでのみます。
items.rubric: Final arrangement: spacious formerly dark room is chosen for reading, with electric light and a clear entrance. Tea remains in the small bright room. Equivalent complete answers may describe both uses. The cupboard problem stays unresolved and does not cancel the room choice.

notes: Original modern Japanese narrative, notices, exercises and deterministic SVGs; no authentic quotations, audio or paid raster generation. Four stages retain the full 40 workbook +8 A +8 B +6 C responses.

The demonstrated G08 subset is polite nonpast i/na adjective predicates and noun modifiers. This chapter does not introduce adjective past/negative paradigms; known verb past is used for the actual chair-borrowing recall. No comparative, superlative, plain-clause or potential paradigm is assumed.

Nine open-slot units stay inside the ceiling: stable ja-09-09 たくさん, ja-09-12 たりません and ja-11-06 つかいます move earlier, with later recall rather than duplicate semantic entries; cupboard, open-result, sit, electric light, switch-on and pull senses support the actual room trial and blocked-door consequence.

The room key remains with Mei. The second parcel is unlocated; the separate delivery sheet and unknown signature remain evidence only. No cupboard contents or map author are invented, and no private letter is opened or read.

Proposed script allocation is 三時半行来: five characters supporting natural whole known spellings 三時 / 半 / 行きます / 来ます. The provisional 日 allocation is deferred: mixed じゅうに日 or さん時 would be unnatural, while full date spellings would need additional characters. This changes no word meaning, narrative target, ceiling or general numeral licence. All story Han retains source-bound authored readings; all other learner Japanese remains kana.

The larger/darker choice has concrete consequences: electric light restores table reading, chairs move without blocking the entrance, and new room-use notices distinguish reading from refreshments. The old cupboard does not open after separate pulls; its internal contents remain unknown.

Parent adopts the bounded G08 nonpast adjective/modifier, seatに, amountたくさん/たりません, use/light/pull and intransitive opening frames shown in the map. No adjective-past/negative, comparative, potential or unseen cardinal series is licensed. The script stage replaces provisional日 with三 to write the known whole clock form naturally, still five new characters;日 is deferred to a later known-word stage. No volume target or lexical ceiling changes.

Parent preflight restores access before a character looks into the previously closed small room, makes printed venue instructions explicit reading/drinking actions, and distinguishes the unknown name field. The early quantity retrieval counts chairs so all three known object-count extras remain grammatical; C5 is an open which-door action question rather than bare yes/no. These are clarity repairs within the same four scenes.
